metadata.title: Equivalence of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-actions on handlebodies of genus $g$

nodes.name: $\mathbf{G}$-action on a handlebody $V_g$
nodes.statement: A {$\mathbf{G}$-action} on a handlebody $V_g$, of genus $g>0$, is a group monomorphism $\phi:{\mathbf{G}}\longrightarrow{}$Homeo$^+(V_g)$, where Homeo$^+(V_g)$ denotes the group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of $V_g$.

nodes.name: equivalence of $\mathbf{G}$-actions on $V_g$
nodes.statement: Two actions $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ on $V_g$ are said to be equivalent if and only if there exists an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h$ of $V_g$ such that $\phi_2(x)=h\circ\phi_1(x)\circ{h^{-1}}$ for all $x\in\mathbf{G}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two actions are equivalent when they are conjugate by an orientation-preserving self-homeomorphism of $V_g$.
differentia: there exists an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h$ of $V_g$ such that $\phi_2(x)=h\circ\phi_1(x)\circ{h^{-1}}$ for all $x\in\mathbf{G}$

nodes.name: graph of groups $(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$ in canonical form and the handlebody orbifold $V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$
nodes.statement: Let v\ $=(r,s,t,m,n)$ be an ordered $5$-tuple of nonnegative integers. The graph of groups $(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$ in canonical form, shown in Figure 1, determines a handlebody orbifold $V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$. The orbifold $V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is constructed in a similar manner as described in \cite{KM}.
nodes.statement_short: A nonnegative $5$-tuple $(r,s,t,m,n)$ indexes a canonical graph of groups, which in turn determines a handlebody orbifold.

nodes.name: generators of the orbifold fundamental group $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)}))$
nodes.statement: We establish notation similar to \cite{KM} and denote the generators of the orbifold fundamental group by $\{a_i: 1\leq{i}\leq{r}\}\cup\{b_j,c_j:1\leq{j}\leq{s}\}\cup\{d_k:1\leq{k}\leq{t}\}\cup\{e_l,f_l:1\leq{l}\leq{m}\}\cup\{g_q:1\leq{q}\leq{n}\}$ such that $b_j^{4}=d_k^{4}=1$, $[b_j,c_j]=1$, $e_l^2=g_q^2=1$, and $[e_l,f_l]=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Fixes the generating set $\{a_i,b_j,c_j,d_k,e_l,f_l,g_q\}$ of the orbifold fundamental group with its torsion and commuting relations.
nodes.definiendum: the generators of the orbifold fundamental group

nodes.name: finite injective epimorphism $\lambda$ onto $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$
nodes.statement: Consider the set of pairs $((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is a finite injective epimorphism from $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ onto $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. We say $\lambda$ is finite injective since the kernel of $\lambda$ is a free group of rank $g$.
nodes.statement_short: An epimorphism $\pi_1^{orb}\to\mathbb{Z}_4$ is called finite injective when its kernel is free of rank $g$.
differentia: the kernel of $\lambda$ is a free group of rank $g$

nodes.name: equivalence relation on pairs $((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Define an equivalence relation on this set of pairs by setting $((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)\equiv(({\Gamma}({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda')$ if and only if there exists an orbifold homeomorphism $h:V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})\longrightarrow{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}$ such that $\lambda'=\lambda\circ{h_*}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two labelled graphs of groups are equivalent when their labellings differ by an orbifold self-homeomorphism.
nodes.definiendum: an equivalence relation on this set of pairs
differentia: there exists an orbifold homeomorphism $h:V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})\longrightarrow{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}$ such that $\lambda'=\lambda\circ{h_*}$

nodes.name: the delta set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$
nodes.statement: We define the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)]$ under this relation.

nodes.name: the set of equivalence classes $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$
nodes.statement: Denote the set set of equivalence classes $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set $\{[\phi]\ |\ \phi:\mathbb{Z}_{4}\longrightarrow{Homeo^+(V_g)}\ and\ V_g/\phi\simeq{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr{E}$ collects the equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$ whose quotient is the given orbifold.

nodes.name: realizable automorphism
nodes.statement: $\alpha$ is realizable $[\alpha=h_*$ for some orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h:V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})\longrightarrow{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}]$
nodes.statement_short: An automorphism is realizable if it is induced by an orientation-preserving self-homeomorphism of the orbifold.

nodes.name: Correspondence between finite group actions on $V_g$ and graphs of groups
nodes.statement: From \cite{MMZ}, the action of any finite group $\mathbf{G}$ on $V_g$ corresponds to a collection of graphs of groups.
assumptions: the action of any finite group $\mathbf{G}$ on $V_g$
conclusions: corresponds to a collection of graphs of groups

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (main theorem: classification and count of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$)
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{Z}_4$ acts on $V_g$, where $g>0$, then $V_g/\mathbb{Z}_4$ is homeomorphic to $V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ for some 5-tuple ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ of nonnegative integers with $r+s+t+m+n>0$ and $g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$. The number of equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$ with this quotient type is $m$ if $r+s+t=0$, and $m+1$ if $r+s+t>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action on $V_g$ has quotient $V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ with $g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$, and the number of classes with that quotient is $m$ or $m+1$.
conclusions: $V_g/\mathbb{Z}_4$ is homeomorphic to $V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ for some 5-tuple ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ of nonnegative integers with $r+s+t+m+n>0$ and $g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$
The number of equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$ with this quotient type is $m$ if $r+s+t=0$, and $m+1$ if $r+s+t>0$.

nodes.name: Corollary 1.2 (even genus forces fixed points)
nodes.statement: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action on a handlebody of even genus must have an interval of fixed points and at least two fixed points on the boundary of the handlebody.
assumptions: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action on a handlebody of even genus
conclusions: must have an interval of fixed points and at least two fixed points on the boundary of the handlebody

nodes.name: Corollary 1.3 (actions free on the boundary)
nodes.statement: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action that is free on the boundary of the handlebody will have $t=n=0$ and $g\equiv1$(mod 4).
assumptions: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action that is free on the boundary of the handlebody

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1 (bijection $\mathscr{E}\leftrightarrow\Delta$)
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$. The set $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}))$ is in one-to-one correspondence with the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ for every $g>0$.
nodes.statement_short: The set of action classes $\mathscr{E}$ is in bijection with the delta set $\Delta$ for every $g>0$.
conclusions: The set $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}))$ is in one-to-one correspondence with the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$

nodes.name: Proposition 2.5 (normalized epimorphisms are equivalent iff $k=k'$)
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ with $m>0$ and let \\$\lambda,\lambda':\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms that satisfy the conclusion of Lemma 2.4, where $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k}$ and $\lambda'(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k'}$. Then $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ if and only if $k=k'$.
nodes.statement_short: Two epimorphisms in the normal form of Lemma 2.4 are equivalent exactly when they send the same number $k$ of generators $f_i$ to $1$.
assumptions: $\lambda,\lambda':\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms that satisfy the conclusion of Lemma 2.4
where $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k}$ and $\lambda'(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k'}$
conclusions: Then $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ if and only if $k=k'$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (generator-hitting epimorphisms are inequivalent)
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ with $m>0$ and let \\$\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that there exists a $j$ with $\lambda_1(f_j)$ being a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ and $\lambda_2(f_i)$ is not a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$. Then $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are not equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda_1$ sends some $f_j$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_4$ but $\lambda_2$ never does, then $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are inequivalent.
assumptions: $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that there exists a $j$ with $\lambda_1(f_j)$ being a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ and $\lambda_2(f_i)$ is not a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$

nodes.name: Lemma 2.4 (normal form for finite injective epimorphisms)
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ and let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism. There exists a finite injective epimorphism $\tilde{\lambda}:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ equivalent to $\lambda$ such that the following hold: \begin{list}{(\arabic{qcounter})~}{\usecounter{qcounter}} \item $\tilde{\lambda}(a_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(a_{r})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(b_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(b_{s})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(c_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{s}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(d_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{t})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(e_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(e_{m})={2}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=1$ for all $i\leq{k}$ some $0\leq{k}\leq{m}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=0$ for all $k<{i}\leq{m}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(g_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{n})=2$. \end{list}
nodes.statement_short: Every finite injective epimorphism is equivalent to one in a normal form prescribing its values on $a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i,e_i,f_i,g_i$.
assumptions: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ and let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism
conclusions: There exists a finite injective epimorphism $\tilde{\lambda}:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ equivalent to $\lambda$ such that the following hold: \begin{list}{(\arabic{qcounter})~}{\usecounter{qcounter}} \item $\tilde{\lambda}(a_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(a_{r})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(b_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(b_{s})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(c_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{s}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(d_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{t})=1$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(e_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(e_{m})={2}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=1$ for all $i\leq{k}$ some $0\leq{k}\leq{m}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=0$ for all $k<{i}\leq{m}$. \item $\tilde{\lambda}(g_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{n})=2$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action class on the genus-2 handlebody
nodes.statement: As we will see, there is exactly one equivalence class of $Z_4$-actions on the handlebody of genus 2.
conclusions: there is exactly one equivalence class of $Z_4$-actions on the handlebody of genus 2

nodes.name: Free-product structure of the orbifold fundamental group
nodes.statement: The orbifold fundamental group of $V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is an extension of $\pi_1(V_g)$ by the group $\mathbf{G}$. We may view the fundamental group as a free product $G_1*G_2*G_3*\cdots*{G_{r+s+t+m+n}}$, where $G_i$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}\times\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$, $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_1^{orb}$ is an extension of $\pi_1(V_g)$ by $\mathbf{G}$ and splits as a free product of $r+s+t+m+n$ factors of five possible types.
conclusions: The orbifold fundamental group of $V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is an extension of $\pi_1(V_g)$ by the group $\mathbf{G}$

We may view the fundamental group as a free product $G_1*G_2*G_3*\cdots*{G_{r+s+t+m+n}}$, where $G_i$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}\times\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$, $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2$

nodes.name: Genus of the covering handlebody from the orbifold Euler characteristic
nodes.statement: Since $V$ is a handlebody with torsion free fundamental group, $V$ is homeomorphic to a handlebody $V_g$ of genus $g=1-4\chi(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$.
assumptions: $V$ is a handlebody with torsion free fundamental group
conclusions: $V$ is homeomorphic to a handlebody $V_g$ of genus $g=1-4\chi(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$

nodes.name: Graphs of groups in canonical form satisfying the normalized conditions
nodes.statement: We may assume these particular graphs of groups are in canonical form and satisfy a set of normalized conditions, which can be found in \cite{KM}.

nodes.name: Restriction to epimorphisms whose kernel is the image of an orbifold covering
nodes.statement: We consider only finite injective epimorphisms such that ker($\lambda$)$=$im($\nu_*$) for some orbifold covering $\nu:V\longrightarrow V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$.

nodes.name: Quotients of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-actions are orbifolds of this type
nodes.statement: Note that the quotient of any $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-action on $V_g$ is an orbifold of this type, up to homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Every $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-action lies in some $\mathscr{E}$
nodes.statement: Note that given any $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-action $\phi:\mathbb{Z}_{4}\longrightarrow{Homeo^+(V_g)}$, it must be the case that for some $V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$, $[\phi]\in\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$.

nodes.name: Fuchs-Rabinovitch generating set for the automorphism group
nodes.statement: Note that from \cite{FR}, a generating set for the automorphisms of the orbifold fundamental group $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)}))$ is the set of mappings $\{\rho_{ji}(x), \lambda_{ji}(x), \mu_{ji}(x), \omega_{ij}, \sigma_i, \phi_i\}$ whose definitions may be found in \cite{FR}. The first five maps are realizable. The realizable $\phi_i$'s are of the form found in Lemma 2.2 and will be used in the remaining arguments of this paper.
nodes.statement_short: The automorphism group is generated by $\{\rho_{ji},\lambda_{ji},\mu_{ji},\omega_{ij},\sigma_i,\phi_i\}$; the first five are always realizable.

nodes.name: The four $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action classes on the genus-3 handlebody $V_3$
nodes.statement: To illustrate the theorem, let $g=3$. Then the genus equation becomes $6=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$ so that $r+s+m$ must equal 0 or 1, and $(r,s,t,m,n)$ is one of $(0,0,2,0,0)$, $(1,0,0,0,1)$, $(0,1,0,0,1)$, or $(0,0,0,1,1)$. Applying Theorem 1.1 to these four possibilities shows that there are a total of $1+1+1+1=4$ equivalence classes of orientation-preserving $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_3$.
nodes.statement_short: For $g=3$ the genus equation admits four $5$-tuples, giving $4$ equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that $\lambda_1$ sends $f_j$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for some $j$ and $\lambda_2$ does not send $f_i$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$. We may assume that ${\lambda_2}(f_i)=0$ for all $i$ by composing $\lambda_2$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{w_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $w_i=0$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$ and $w_i=1$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=2$. To show that $\lambda_1$ and ${\lambda_2}$ are not equivalent we will consider the element $f_j$ such that $\lambda_1(f_j)$ generates $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. For contradiction, assume that $\lambda_1$ is equivalent to ${\lambda_2}$. Then by Lemma \ref{real}, there exists a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $\alpha(f_j)=ue_m^wf_m^{\pm1}u^{-1}$, where $u\in{\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma(}$v${),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))}$ and $0\leq{w}<{2}$. Hence $\lambda_1(f_j)=w{\lambda_2}(e_m)$, where ${\lambda_2}(e_m)$ is a multiple of $2$, and hence $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a multiple of $2$. This is impossible since $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. Therefore $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ cannot be equivalent, proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: normalize $\lambda_2$ so that $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$, then Lemma 2.2 forces $\lambda_1(f_j)$ to be a multiple of $2$, contradicting that it generates $\mathbb{Z}_4$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism. Properties (5) and (8) must occur since $\lambda$ is finite injective. Property (4) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism \\$\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $d_i$ to the element $d_i^{{\varepsilon}_i}$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $\varepsilon_i=1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=1$ and $\varepsilon_i=-1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=3$. Property (2) follows by a similar technique. Assuming property (2) holds, property (3) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $c_i$ to the element $b_i^{-\lambda(c_i)}c_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. To show properties (6) and (7) hold, we may compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{z_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $z_i=1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=2$, $z_i=2$ if $\lambda(f_i)=0$ or $\lambda(f_i)=1$, and $z_i=-1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=3$. Furthermore, composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphisms $\omega_{ij}$ we may interchange $f_i$ as needed so that the first $k$ generators map to 1 and the last $m-k$ generators map to 0. Finally, to prove property (1) we may assume that there exists an element $x\in G_j$ (where $G_j$ is either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, $\mathbb{Z}_4\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$) such that $\lambda(x)=1$. Note that we may compose $\lambda$ with a realizable automorphism that sends $x$ to $x^{-1}$ if needed. Now compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\rho_{ji}(x^{-\lambda(a_i)+1})$. It may be shown that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(a_i)=1$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Establish the eight normal-form properties one at a time by composing $\lambda$ with suitable realizable automorphisms.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement: For a contradiction, assume that $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ and $k\neq{k'}$. Without loss of generality we may assume that $k>k'$. Hence, $\lambda$ maps at least one more generator $f_i$ to 1 as does $\lambda'$. This would mean that there must exist a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(f_{k'+1})=0$. By Lemma 2.2, this is impossible. Thus, $k=k'$. For the reverse implication suppose that $k=k'$. Then $\lambda=\lambda'$, proving the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction on $k>k'$ using Lemma 2.2, then the immediate reverse implication $k=k'\Rightarrow\lambda=\lambda'$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Define $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. Define $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for at least one $i$ such that $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. By Lemma 2.3, the delta set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ is the disjoint union $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\dot{\bigcup}\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Hence, the order of the delta set is the sum of the orders of the two sets $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ and $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Applying Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5, $|\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=m$ and \\$|\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=1$. Hence by Proposition 2.1, the theorem follows.
nodes.statement_short: Split the delta set into $\Delta_0\dot\cup\Delta_1$, count $|\Delta_1|=m$ and $|\Delta_0|=1$, then transfer the count through the bijection of Proposition 2.1.

nodes.name: Set up the two epimorphisms
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that $\lambda_1$ sends $f_j$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for some $j$ and $\lambda_2$ does not send $f_i$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\lambda_1$ hitting a generator on some $f_j$ and $\lambda_2$ never hitting one.

nodes.name: Normalize $\lambda_2$ so that $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$
nodes.statement: We may assume that ${\lambda_2}(f_i)=0$ for all $i$ by composing $\lambda_2$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{w_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $w_i=0$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$ and $w_i=1$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=2$.
nodes.statement_short: Compose $\lambda_2$ with the realizable $\prod\phi_i$ to make all $\lambda_2(f_i)$ vanish.

nodes.name: Assume equivalence for contradiction
nodes.statement: To show that $\lambda_1$ and ${\lambda_2}$ are not equivalent we will consider the element $f_j$ such that $\lambda_1(f_j)$ generates $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. For contradiction, assume that $\lambda_1$ is equivalent to ${\lambda_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Single out $f_j$ with $\lambda_1(f_j)$ a generator and suppose the two are equivalent.

nodes.name: Apply the realizability criterion of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma \ref{real}, there exists a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $\alpha(f_j)=ue_m^wf_m^{\pm1}u^{-1}$, where $u\in{\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma(}$v${),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))}$ and $0\leq{w}<{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.2 pins the form $\alpha(f_j)=ue_m^wf_m^{\pm1}u^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Derive the parity contradiction
nodes.statement: Hence $\lambda_1(f_j)=w{\lambda_2}(e_m)$, where ${\lambda_2}(e_m)$ is a multiple of $2$, and hence $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a multiple of $2$. This is impossible since $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. Therefore $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ cannot be equivalent, proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda_1(f_j)$ must then be a multiple of $2$, so it cannot generate $\mathbb{Z}_4$.

nodes.name: Fix a finite injective epimorphism $\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Start from an arbitrary finite injective epimorphism.

nodes.name: Properties (5) and (8) from finite injectivity
nodes.statement: Properties (5) and (8) must occur since $\lambda$ is finite injective.
nodes.statement_short: The values on the $e_i$ and $g_i$ are forced to be $2$.

nodes.name: Property (4) via sign-flipping automorphisms
nodes.statement: Property (4) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism \\$\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $d_i$ to the element $d_i^{{\varepsilon}_i}$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $\varepsilon_i=1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=1$ and $\varepsilon_i=-1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=3$.
nodes.statement_short: Compose with $\phi_i:d_i\mapsto d_i^{\varepsilon_i}$ to make every $\lambda(d_i)=1$.

nodes.name: Property (2) by the same technique
nodes.statement: Property (2) follows by a similar technique.
nodes.statement_short: Normalizes $\lambda(b_i)$.

nodes.name: Property (3) by absorbing $b_i$-powers into $c_i$
nodes.statement: Assuming property (2) holds, property (3) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $c_i$ to the element $b_i^{-\lambda(c_i)}c_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed.
nodes.statement_short: Compose with $\phi_i:c_i\mapsto b_i^{-\lambda(c_i)}c_i$ to kill $\lambda(c_i)$.

nodes.name: Properties (6) and (7) by normalizing and permuting the $f_i$
nodes.statement: To show properties (6) and (7) hold, we may compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{z_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $z_i=1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=2$, $z_i=2$ if $\lambda(f_i)=0$ or $\lambda(f_i)=1$, and $z_i=-1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=3$. Furthermore, composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphisms $\omega_{ij}$ we may interchange $f_i$ as needed so that the first $k$ generators map to 1 and the last $m-k$ generators map to 0.
nodes.statement_short: Adjust each $f_i$ by $e_i^{z_i}$, then permute with $\omega_{ij}$ so the first $k$ map to $1$.

nodes.name: Property (1) via the $\rho_{ji}$ automorphisms
nodes.statement: Finally, to prove property (1) we may assume that there exists an element $x\in G_j$ (where $G_j$ is either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, $\mathbb{Z}_4\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$) such that $\lambda(x)=1$. Note that we may compose $\lambda$ with a realizable automorphism that sends $x$ to $x^{-1}$ if needed. Now compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\rho_{ji}(x^{-\lambda(a_i)+1})$. It may be shown that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(a_i)=1$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $x$ with $\lambda(x)=1$ and compose with $\prod\rho_{ji}(x^{-\lambda(a_i)+1})$ to send every $a_i$ to $1$.

nodes.name: Assume equivalence with $k\neq k'$
nodes.statement: For a contradiction, assume that $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ and $k\neq{k'}$. Without loss of generality we may assume that $k>k'$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$ are equivalent while $k>k'$.

nodes.name: Contradict Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Hence, $\lambda$ maps at least one more generator $f_i$ to 1 as does $\lambda'$. This would mean that there must exist a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(f_{k'+1})=0$. By Lemma 2.2, this is impossible. Thus, $k=k'$.
nodes.statement_short: A realizable $\alpha$ would have to send $f_{k'+1}$ to $0$, which Lemma 2.2 forbids.

nodes.name: Reverse implication
nodes.statement: For the reverse implication suppose that $k=k'$. Then $\lambda=\lambda'$, proving the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: If $k=k'$ the two epimorphisms coincide.

nodes.name: Define the subsets $\Delta_0$ and $\Delta_1$ of the delta set
nodes.statement: Define $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. Define $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for at least one $i$ such that $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the classes by whether all $\lambda(f_i)=0$ or some $\lambda(f_i)=1$.

nodes.name: Delta set is the disjoint union, so the orders add
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.3, the delta set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ is the disjoint union $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\dot{\bigcup}\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Hence, the order of the delta set is the sum of the orders of the two sets $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ and $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.3 makes the union disjoint, so $|\Delta|=|\Delta_0|+|\Delta_1|$.

nodes.name: Count the two parts
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5, $|\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=m$ and \\$|\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5 give $|\Delta_1|=m$ and $|\Delta_0|=1$.

nodes.name: Transfer the count through Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: Hence by Proposition 2.1, the theorem follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude via the bijection.
